problem: Multiview scene representations resolve occlusions for navigation but require pooling raw camera data, exposing private information (e.g. identities) from every camera to a trusted third party or to other parties.
motivation: Large cluttered environments have occluded obstacles that a single egocentric view cannot resolve, so cameras must be combined. Ubiquitous cameras make privacy a serious concern, so the combined representation should be usable only for the navigation output and nothing else (e.g. not face recognition).
key_idea: Run the action-prediction network under secure multiparty computation (arithmetic secret sharing via CrypTen) over features from the agent's view, a map, and external cameras, so no party learns anything beyond the predicted actions.
insight: Camera views add large accuracy gains over map-only and first-person baselines, since hidden obstacles are otherwise unobservable. Encryption costs under 1-2% accuracy relative to plaintext (2-party 96.6% and 5-party 96.9% vs plaintext 97.1%). A linear probe predicting obstacle presence reaches 49.7% on encrypted features versus 93.6% on plaintext features, consistent with the privacy guarantee. The price is inference overhead of roughly 500x (2-party) to 1500x (5-party) on GPU.
method: Problem formulation: predict the next discrete action (N/S/E/W/stay, 5-dim one-hot) from the agent's egocentric view o, a public 5x5 map m, and n fixed camera images c_i
Arithmetic secret sharing: each encoded feature is split into P additive shares mod Q, and the action network G operates on the shares, so F = sum_p G([C]_p,[O]_p,[M]_p) mod Q

Two-stage training: the view encoder (2 conv + 2 linear) and map encoder (3 linear) are pretrained in plaintext and computed locally; then the 4-layer MLP action head G is trained from scratch under MPC with the encoders frozen
MSE loss instead of cross-entropy: log and exp are hard to approximate in MPC and cause non-convergence and overflow; ReLU is the only activation used; a stop token masks later steps
Multi-party settings: 2-party (all cameras owned by one party plus the agent) and 5-party (each camera and the agent a separate party), semi-honest security via CrypTen
Obstacle World dataset: built on Gym MiniWorld with 12 map layouts, 1-3 random obstacles, 4 corner cameras plus the agent's view; BFS ground-truth paths, balanced 50% detour / 50% no-detour

setting.backbone: Small CNN view encoder + MLP map encoder + 4-layer MLP action classifier (trained from scratch; head trained under MPC with CrypTen)
setting.training_data: Obstacle World: 15,000 training environments with BFS ground-truth action sequences (teacher forcing); 2,250 test environments generated on the fly
setting.observation: egocentric 45x60 RGB view, 5x5 discrete map, plus 4 fixed external camera RGB views
setting.privileged: Fixed external cameras giving full observability of obstacles (encrypted via secret sharing); public map; no other privileged information

numbers.backbone: CNN/MLP encoders + MLP action head under CrypTen
numbers.extra: agent and cameras encrypted via secret sharing; encoders pretrained in plaintext
numbers.evidence: Table 1: 2-party MPC w/ Camera Views 93.6% / 98.8% / 96.6%; efficiency table 99.5%

numbers.backbone: CNN/MLP encoders + MLP action head under CrypTen
numbers.extra: each camera is a separate party
numbers.evidence: Table 1: 5-party MPC w/ Camera Views 94.3% / 99.2% / 96.9%; efficiency table 99.2%

numbers.method: Plaintext w/ Camera Views (non-private upper bound)
numbers.backbone: CNN/MLP encoders + MLP action head, plaintext
numbers.extra: no privacy; trusted third party sees all data

numbers_note: Obstacle World is the paper's own new synthetic benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark; the metric is action-sequence success accuracy. Results are reported as a single run, without error bars.
results: On the new Obstacle World, 2-party and 5-party MPC reach 96.6% and 96.9% overall accuracy versus 97.1% for the plaintext non-private upper bound. The strongest privacy-preserving baseline without cameras, First Person (deterministic start), reaches 88.8%; map-only reaches 74.0%. Forward-pass overhead is about 500x for 2-party and 1500x for 5-party on GPU.
limitations: Only a small synthetic grid world with fixed cameras and a static environment; no real-world or standard benchmark evaluation
MPC adds large inference overhead (500-1500x) and needs low-latency network communication; semi-honest security only, and outputs still leak obstacle locations via repeated queries
Memoryless per-step prediction causes oscillation and conflicts between map and camera cues; long multi-turn detours fail
